intro: Recycling work builds machine operation, monitoring and quality checks, skills used across plants and job sites. The closest of the 25 careers below is Packaging and Filling Machine Operators and Tenders, with a 90% skill match, and every option needs no extra schooling.
why_it_works: Sorting and processing material means running balers and conveyors, spotting what does not belong and keeping lines safe. O*NET rates operation and control at 3.25 out of 5 for this job and operations monitoring at 3.12. Production, hazardous materials and mining work use the same habits. BLS does not publish a separate pay figure for this job, so this page lists medians instead of percent changes.
tips: Get a forklift or equipment operator certificate; it opens many plant and warehouse jobs.
Refinery operators earn $96,710 and are a 78% match, one of the best-paid options here.
Hazardous Materials Removal Workers earn $49,450 and value your safety habits.

faq.q: What jobs can former recycling workers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are packaging and filling machine operators (90%), Hazardous Materials Removal Workers (88%) and production helpers (84%), based on O*NET 31.0. Tire Builders are also 81% matched, with a BLS median of $57,390, and need no extra education.

faq.q: Which jobs for recycling workers pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are refinery operators at $96,710, mining roof bolters at $78,540 and rail-track equipment operators at $70,070, according to BLS May 2025 data. BLS has no separate figure for recycling workers, so compare these with your pay.

faq.q: Do recycling workers need a degree to switch jobs?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than recycling and reclamation workers already have. In the closest match, 80% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and a certification, such as forklift or hazmat training, can help for some plant jobs.

faq.q: What skills should recycling workers build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are repairing, complex problem solving, equipment maintenance and operations analysis. Quality control already rates 2.75 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so learning to fix the machines you run is the main step up.
